meta.revision: ios-2026-07-26 — restyled to an Apple HIG-flavoured system. Structure, token NAMES and the reserved verdict semantics are unchanged, so every component that already reads tokens inherits the new look with no edit of its own. Only values moved.

font.heading: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Display', 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', var(--font-body-fallback), 'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif
font.body: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'SF Pro Display', 'Segoe UI', var(--font-body-fallback), 'Noto Sans Devanagari', sans-serif
font.note: San Francisco is served by the OS on Apple hardware — the most faithful way to feel like iOS, and it costs zero network requests. Inter loads as the cross-platform fallback through --font-body-fallback. Devanagari fallback retained for the PH2 Hindi requirement.

type.label: 12px/1.4
type.note: Mirrors the iOS text styles (footnote 13 · subheadline 15 · body 17 · title3 20 · title2 22 · title1 28). Body moves 14px -> 15px: still dense enough for 44px table rows, materially more readable. Negative tracking at display sizes is what makes SF look like SF.

radius.note: Apple's continuous-corner geometry reads as generous. 10px on controls, 16px on cards, 20px on sheets.

elevation.note: Two-layer shadows — a tight contact shadow plus a wide soft one. One blurred shadow reads as Material, not Apple.

motion.note: The curve approximates a critically-damped iOS spring: quick to leave, slow to settle. Every use degrades under prefers-reduced-motion.

material.note: Translucency is for CHROME ONLY — sidebar, toolbars, sheets. Data surfaces stay opaque. iOS does the same, and frosting a dense compliance table costs contrast (WCAG) and paint time for no gain.

semantics.note: Verdict hues are reserved — never repurposed for non-verdict UI. Values are the iOS system green/red/orange darkened until each passes 4.5:1 on its own tint; the raw system colours do not.
